page: Google Cloud Platform n2-highmem-4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance belonging to the N2 server family. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores of an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.8 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The hardware configuration includes 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. This instance does not include local storage or bundled GPU accelerators, and it provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark evaluations indicate that the n2-highmem-4 exhibits modest processing capabilities. Both single-core and multi-core CPU performance under stress-ng fall into the bottom 25% tier. Similarly, Geekbench single-core and multi-core scores are positioned in the weak category, with software compilation and ray tracing benchmarks matching this tier. Memory bandwidth tests for both small cached blocks and large uncached blocks also register in the bottom 25%, though the PassMark memory score achieves an average rating. Single-threaded gzip compression performs at an average level, whereas multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and image processing drop to the bottom 10%.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the n2-highmem-4 offers high memory density per vCPU, making it suitable for memory-bound workloads that do not require intense CPU throughput. The tradeoff involves lower computational and memory bandwidth performance relative to the allocated RAM capacity. This instance is suited for small-scale database operations, caching layers, and memory-intensive enterprise applications that operate within moderate CPU utilization thresholds.
